newsitem.title: USA: Johnson & Johnson's Nicotrol gets FDA approval.
newsitem.headline: Johnson & Johnson's Nicotrol gets FDA approval.

text.p: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration cleared the Nicotrol Inhaler nicotine inhalation system for prescription sale, a unit of Johnson & Johnson said Monday.

McNeil Consumer Products Co. said the Inhaler is the first form of nicotine replacement therapy to help control a smoker's cravings for cigarettes while satisfying the need for a key behavioural component of smoking, the hand-to-mouth ritual, which a smoker may repeat up to 73,000 times each year.
The inhaler provides nicotine, but at a lower level than cigarettes, so that smokers can alleviate their need for nicotine, McNeil said.
The company said that the current nicotine replacement products -- patch, gum, and nasal spray -- are designed to address physical cravings.

But many smokers also complain that they miss the cigarette and all the behaviours that go with it, like taking it out of the pack, lighting it, putting it to the lips, sucking, inhaling and holding it, McNeil said.
